1.
Personal affidavit filed by respondent no. 3 and counter affidavit filed by the petitioners in reply thereto, are taken on record.

2. The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus commanding the respondent-Authorities to consider the claim of the petitioners for payment of sale consideration amount according to circle rate, i.e. Rs. 28 lakhs per hectare, which was applicable on the date of execution of the sale deeds by the petitioners in favour of the respondents and for a further direction to respondent no. 2 to take appropriate decision on the application of the petitioners dated 18.3.2024.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The case of the petitioners is that the land of the petitioners and adjoining land were required by U.P. Expressway Industrial Development Authority for construction of expressway.
It offered to purchase the land of the petitioners in terms of G.O. dated 19.3.2015.
The petitioners agreed to the same and accordingly they transferred some part of their land required by respondent no. 2 by means of different sale deeds executed in the year 2021.

The circle rate at the relevant time was Rs.
20 lakhs per hectare and as per G.O. dated 19.3.2015, the petitioners were paid four times the circle rate as sale consideration amount at the time of obtaining sale deed from them in the year 2021.
4. The further case of the petitioners is that while executing the project, the second respondent utilized certain additional land of the petitioners.
The petitioners requested the Authorities to demarcate their holding and pay compensation for the extra land utilized by them.
However, when no heed was paid to their request, they were compelled to approach this court by means of Writ - C No. 23747 of 2022.

It was disposed of by a Co-ordinate Division Bench on 14.11.2022, directing the State respondents to carry out demarcation of the land of the petitioners and in case in demarcation it is found that any extra land has been utilized, the Development Authority would pay compensation for the same.
5.
The case of the petitioners it that thereafter, the respondents, admitting that they had taken extra land, approached the petitioners for obtaining sale deed for the excess area.

The petitioners executed sale deeds on 7.12.2023 and 11.12.2023, but they were paid sale consideration at the same rate, i.e. Rs. 20 lakhs per hectare, although by that time, there had been revision of the circle rate and it was enhanced to Rs. 28 lakhs per hectare.
6.

On 11.9.2024, the following order was passed: -
"1. The sale-deed obtained by the respondents from the petitioners discloses the prevailing circle rate as Rs.20,00,000/- per hectare whereas according to the petitioners, it was Rs.28,00,000/- per hectare at the relevant time.

2. Let respondent No. 3 clarify the said aspect by filing his affidavit.
3. List as fresh on 30 September 2024.
4.
Learned standing counsel undertakes to communicate the instant order to the concerned officer for due compliance."

7. In compliance of the said order, respondent no. 3 has filed her personal affidavit and in which it is admitted that the sale deed was obtained from the petitioners for additional area as per the provisions of G.O. dated 19.3.2015.
It is also admitted in the said affidavit that the circle rate was enhanced to Rs. 28 lakhs per hectare from 1.4.2023.

Thus, on the date sale deed in relation to additional area was obtained from the petitioners, the circle rate was Rs. 28 lakhs per hectare, but the sale deed was obtained by mentioning the circle rate to be Rs. 20 lakhs per hectare.
The stand taken in the counter affidavit is that the petitioners willingly accepted the said amount.

entities.text: Malook Singh And 3 Others vs State Of Up And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners only gave consent for transfer of their land at the prescribed circle rate.

Since there was delay in obtaining the sale deed and by that time the circle rate had been revised, therefore, the circle rate, as applicable on the date of execution of the sale deed, should have been applied.

The respondents, taking advantage of the ignorance of the petitioners, wrongly mentioned in the sale deed that circle rate at that time was Rs.20 lakh per hectare, although admittedly, by that time, it was enhanced to Rs.28 lakh per hectare.

9. It is further submitted that in the alternative, in case the respondents are treating the second set of sales as continuation of the initial sale, then the petitioners were entitled to interest from December, 2021 upto December, 2023, i.e. the interval between the two set of sales.
10. Concededly, G.O. dated 19.3.2015 provides for obtaining land of private individuals on basis of mutual agreement at the circle rate prevalent at particular point of time.

Since the respondents had utilized the land of the petitioners without acquisition and after intervention by this court,
demarcation was held and wherein it transpired that extra land had been utilized and the respondents thereafter obtained sale deed from the petitioners, the claim of the petitioners for payment of interest from the year 2021 until the sale deed for the extra land was actually obtained,
is held to be lawful and sustainable.
11. Had the respondents acquired the land under the provisions of Act No. 30 of 2013, the respondents would have issued preliminary notification and date of issuing the said notification would have been the relevant date for determining compensation for the additional land.
In that event, the amount would have been much higher.

12. In such circumstances, we are of the opinion that the alternative submission of counsel for the petitioners for payment of interest to them by treating the second set of sales as transactions done in continuation of the first set of sales is liable to be accepted.

Accordingly, we allow interest @ 9% per annum for the first year to be calculated from the date of execution of the first set of sales and @
15% per annum for period thereafter, until the date of payment of the sale consideration amount, by applying the analogy of Section 80 of Act No. 30 of 2013.

13. Learned counsel for respondent no. 2 submits that respondent no. 2 would make available necessary funds to respondent no. 4 within four weeks from the date the amount payable to the petitioners is intimated to it by respondent no. 4.
14.

Accordingly, the petition is disposed of by providing that respondent no. 2 will calculate the amount of interest payable to the petitioners within two weeks from the date of communication of the instant order.
Respondent no. 2 will make available the required funds to respondent no. 4 within four weeks thence.
Respondent no. 4 will release the amount in favour of the petitioners within next two weeks.

(Manish Kumar Nigam, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 30.9.2024 Jaideep/-
